Tested the actual native WebKit browser, including the local page currently open at port 8080. A simple long document scrolls at about 16.7 ms per frame. The rich Super landing page takes roughly 247–421 ms per measured frame in these trials. Turning on compositing with the legacy renderer did not solve it. Pausing its WebGL animation while scrolling reduced drawing to one call during the measured interval, but scrolling remained slow. Git review requires the native-selected repository and matching selection generation. Each Git read has a 10-second deadline and a 512 KiB output limit. The list shows at most 1,000 changes; rendered patches cap lines/line lengths with a visible notice. External diff/text conversion and optional index locks are disabled. Text reads retain the editor's file restrictions. Binary/special files and oversize contents produce a visible refusal. A deleted file whose parent folder is itself gone is not yet reviewable here. Git status and patches are successive disk snapshots, not an atomic acceptance basis; refresh when external tools change files.
